title: Christmas festivities slowly return to West Bank holy city of Bethlehem
summary: The city of Bethlehem prepares to hold Christmas as celebrations are slowly returning to the holy land after celebrations were called off in the past two years due to the Israel-Hamas war. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Jerusalem, Noga Tarnopolsky.

title: Ukraine: Zelensky reveals revised 20-point US plan to end Russian war
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has revealed details of the latest US-led plan to end the war in Ukraine, saying it had been agreed between negotiators from Kyiv and Washington and sent to Moscow for feedback. Analysis by Stefan Wolff, professor of international security at the University of Birmingham. Story by Carys Garland.

title: After football World Cup exit and coaching shake-up, Cameroon braces for AFCON challenge
summary: After failing to qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup and sacking their coach just weeks before AFCON, Cameroon's national football team is facing an uphill battle ahead of their opening game against Gabon on Wednesday. But newly appointed coach David Pagou says he's up for the challenge. Story by Laurent Berstecher.

title: French Christmas traditions, from foie gras to oysters and the bûche de Noël
summary: Christmas dinner in France makes good on a promise to dine very well, offering everything from extravagant seafood platters to sweet treats such as the traditional Yule log cake (or bûche de Noël). Here are some of the delicacies you might find at a traditional French holiday feast.

title: To boycott or not to boycott? Ivory Coast holds tense parliamentary election
summary: Supporters of former Ivorian president Laurent Gbagbo are divided over whether to boycott the country’s upcoming parliamentary elections. The disagreement follows the recent presidential election, in which incumbent President Alassane Ouattara won a controversial fourth term after Gbagbo was barred from running. title: Youth's vote crucial in upcoming Central African Republic general election
summary: General elections are due to be held in the Central African Republic on December 28. It is the first time in decades that the election includes presidential, parliamentary and municipal elections. With almost 82% of young people unemployed, the youth hope a change in government might boost job opportunities and economic growth. Report by Jospin Bissi, Cyril…

title: Sudan PM presents peace plan at UN, calling for a ceasefire
summary: Sudan's Prime Minister has brought a wide ranging peace plan before the United Nations. But the paramilitary group, the Rapid Support Forces, has yet to sign onto it, and experts say it is unlikely they will, as it demands their withdrawal and disarmament. Story by Ellen Gainsford.

title: In Japan, bears have gone from dangerous to delicious
summary: Since Japan recorded a spike in deadly bear attacks, some restaurants have struggled to keep up with booming demand for grilled cuts of the animal. Cooked on a stone slate – or in a hot pot with vegetables – the meat comes from bears culled to curb maulings that have killed a record 13 people this year. Story by Gabrielle Nadler.

title: France slams US visa ban as row over European 'censorship' deepens
summary: France condemned on Wednesday a US visa ban on Thierry Breton, a former European Union commissioner who helped drive landmark online regulation that Washington believes censors free speech and unfairly targets US tech giants. title: Zelensky unveils new US-backed, 20-point plan to end the war in Ukraine
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Wednesday revealed details of the latest US-backed 20-point plan to end the war in Ukraine, saying it has been sent to Moscow for feedback. Zelensky gave a point-by-point briefing to journalists in Kyiv, including details on the creation of demilitarised zones.

title: Christmas in Ukraine: 'Despite the war, our children want to feel happy'
summary: Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky says he's hoping for an answer from Moscow on Wednesday to the draft peace plan hashed out between Washington and Kyiv. Meanwhile, the president's compatriots are preparing to celebrate yet another Christmas under Russian invasion. title: Fresh Epstein files release contains multiple Trump references
summary: A new batch of Jeffrey Epstein files released Tuesday contains numerous references to President Donald Trump, including documents detailing flights he took on his then friend's private jet, and other claims that his Justice Department described as "untrue and sensationalist." Story by Camille Knight.

title: Christmas celebrations in Kenya: Families spend on average one month's salary
summary: In Kenya, Christmas is primarily a religious celebration that brings families together. As summer approaches and temperatures rise, Santa Claus and Christmas trees are relatively rare. But that does not mean people don’t celebrate — the day is usually marked by generous meals on December 25th. Report by Elodie Cousin and Bastien Renouil.

title: Libya army chief of staff killed in jet crash near Ankara after fault reported
summary: A private jet that crashed overnight, killing Libya's army chief of staff and seven others on board, had reported an electrical fault and requested an emergency landing ​shortly before contact was lost, a Turkish official said on Wednesday. Story by Charlotte Lam.

title: Thailand - Cambodia peace talks in doubt over venue row
summary: Thailand on Tuesday rejected a request by Cambodia to hold bilateral talks in a neutral country, leaving a planned meeting to negotiate an end to deadly border clashes in doubt. The nations' long-standing border conflict reignited this month, shattering an earlier truce, killing more than 40 people and displacing over 900,000 on both sides, officials said.…

title: Christmas celebrations slowly return to Bethlehem, Jesus' birthplace
summary: Christmas celebrations in Bethlehem, Jesus’ traditional birthplace, are slowly returning, as the city in the Israeli-occupied West Bank emerges from the shadow of war to celebrate its first festive Christmas in more than two years. Story by Bryan Quinn.

title: Venezuela accuses US of 'extortion' and seeks to criminalise oil tanker seizures
summary: Venezuela’s parliament on Tuesday approved a measure that criminalises a broad range of activities that can hinder navigation and commerce in the South American country, such as the seizure of oil tankers. summary: In southern Moscow three people, including two police officers, were killed by an overnight explosion, Russian authorities said on Wednesday. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said a new 20-point plan, agreed on by US and Ukrainian negotiators, was being reviewed by Moscow. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

title: US accused of “greatest extortion known in our history” over Venezuela at UN
summary: Russia and China sharply criticized the United States at the UN Security Council on Tuesday over its military and economic pressure on Venezuela, accusing Washington of intimidation and violations of international law as tensions over sanctions and a naval blockade escalated.

title: US bars five Europeans over alleged pressure on tech firms to censor speech
summary: The US State Department said Tuesday that it has barred five Europeans accused of leading efforts to pressure US technology companies into censoring or suppressing American viewpoints, in a move that sharpens tensions with European regulators over online speech.

title: Supreme Court blocks Trump’s National Guard deployment in Chicago
summary: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday halted President Donald Trump’s attempt to deploy National Guard troops in Chicago, dealing a setback to his immigration crackdown and raising fresh questions about the limits of presidential authority to use the military for domestic law enforcement.

title: Ukraine withdraws troops from eastern town amid deadly Russian strikes
summary: Ukraine said on Tuesday it had pulled its forces out of a hard-fought eastern town as Russia stepped up air strikes that killed civilians, knocked out power supplies and underlined the lack of progress in diplomatic efforts to end the war ahead of Christmas.

title: Pope calls for Christmas Day truce, laments Russia’s rejection
summary: Pope Leo XIV on Tuesday renewed his call for a worldwide truce on Christmas Day, expressing sadness that Russia had apparently rejected the appeal, as fighting in Ukraine raged on, civilians were killed in Russian air strikes, and diplomatic efforts involving the United States and Europe showed little sign of a breakthrough.

title: AFCON: Lookman strike gives Nigeria winning start against Tanzania
summary: Nigeria began their Africa Cup of Nations Group C campaign with three points on Tuesday as Ademola Lookman’s long-range effort settled a rain-soaked contest against Tanzania in Fes, easing the Super Eagles past stubborn opposition despite missed chances and a brief second-half scare.

summary: France's internal intelligence services are investigating a cyberattack on the country's national postal service that has disrupted deliveries during the busy Christmas season. title: Sudan's prime minister takes his peace plan to the UN
summary: In tonight's edition, Sudan's prime minister urged members of the United Nations Security Council to stand “on the right side of history" as he laid out his plan to end the war in Sudan. Also, voters gear up to head to the polls in the Central African Republic for historic elections. And in Kenya, Christmas is a season rooted in faith, family, and food.

title: Libyan army chief of staff found dead in plane wreckage, PM says
summary: Libyan military chief Muhammad Ali Ahmad al Haddad and four others died in a plane crash in Turkey on Tuesday evening, Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah has confirmed. Turkey's air traffic controllers lost contact with a jet carrying the Libyan delegation that was heading home after a visit to Ankara, the Turkish interior minister said.

title: Brazil's Supreme Court allows Bolsonaro to leave prison for surgery on Christmas
summary: Brazil's Supreme Court granted a request by ex-president Jair Bolsonaro to leave prison to undergo surgery on Christmas for a hernia. Bolsonaro is currently serving a 27-year sentence after being convicted of plotting a coup to remain in power.

title: Senegal gets its AFCON 2025 campaign started with victory over Botswana
summary: A Nicolas Jackson double has helped Senegal get its Africa Cup of Nations campaign off to a winning start, defeating Botswana 3-0 in Tangier. Senegal, the winner of the AFCON 2021, was the hot favourite going into the match against a team ranked 138th in the world.

title: What makes a hit song? How to keep it real in the age of AI
summary: There's nothing more innately human than humming a tune. Especially when it's made by humans. But don't bother trying to see The Velvet Sundown in concert: the band doesn't exist. The sounds are produced with artificial intelligence.

title: Russia attacks Ukraine energy sector with drones and missiles strikes
summary: Russia fired more than 650 drones and three dozen missiles at Ukraine in a large-scale attack that began during the night and stretched into daylight hours Tuesday, officials said. At least three people were killed, including a 4-year-old child, two days before Christmas.

title: Nonstop laughing for 20 minutes: Japan’s ritual for good fortune
summary: Every winter in Osaka, thousands gather at a temple to laugh—nonstop—for 20 minutes. Known as "Owarai Shinji", this rare ritual draws on ancient Japanese mythology, where laughter once brought the sun back to the world. More than humor, they see it as a disciplined act of unity, hope, and renewal.

title: Louvre installs metal bars over infamous gallery window after $102M jewel heist
summary: The Louvre Museum has installed a large metal grille over the windows of the gallery from which thieves stole jewellery worth an estimated $102 million. The bars are the latest measure put in place in recent month as the security standards at the world's most visited museum are facing intense scrutiny following the October heist.

title: Australian PM Albanese to invite Israeli President Herzog following anti-Semitic attack
summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese on Tuesday said that his government would invite Israeli President Isaac Herzog to visit Australia following a deadly anti-Semitic shooting in Sydney targeting the Jewish community.
